title: Coherent global sections over a valuation ring
statement: Let A be a valuation ring, let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be proper, flat, and of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let F be an invertible module on X [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then H^0(X,F) is a finitely presented A-module.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, proof using coherence of valuation rings and coherent cohomology

proof.text: By [def-sc-invertible-module], an invertible module is locally free of rank one. Thus it satisfies the locally-free finite-rank hypothesis of [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] with d=1, which is the coefficient hypothesis of the valuation-ring coherent higher-direct-image statement.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0EX8, setup of the coherent module F

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-valuation-proper-coherent-higher-direct-images] with q=0. Its conclusion says that H^0(X,F) is a finitely presented A-module, which is the asserted statement.
